Expected interpretation: Ingredient: chicken (required). Meal: dinner (required). Quality: quick (rank only)
Expected result: 2-3 dinner mains containing chicken
Must never happen: Non-dinner results; a hard time cutoff applied from the word "quick" alone
Why this case: Baseline discovery. Everything else varies from this.

Expected interpretation: Quality: comforting (rank only). No meal type stated
Expected result: 2-3 recipes across meal types
Must never happen: Forcing dinner when the user never said dinner
Why this case: Unspecified meal type stays unspecified.

Expected interpretation: Meal: dinner (required). Time: 30 min (required - a number filters)
Expected result: 2-3 dinner mains at or under 30 minutes
Must never happen: A 35-minute recipe appearing
Why this case: A number is a hard filter even though time is normally a ranking signal.

User says: I need snacks for my son's soccer team after practice
Expected interpretation: Situation: crowd of kids; portable; no utensils; fast
Expected result: 2-3 portable crowd snacks
Must never happen: Literal phrase search; a single-serving fussy recipe; excluding everything untagged kid-friendly
Why this case: Dale's case. Tests situational interpretation.

Expected interpretation: Quality: familiar and approachable (rank only)
Expected result: 2-3 approachable recipes
Must never happen: Searching the literal string "picky eaters"
Why this case: Interpretation vs keyword matching.

Expected interpretation: Situation: crowd serving
Expected result: 2-3 crowd recipes
Must never happen: Single-serving recipes
Why this case: Tests that ambiguous occasion words resolve to a serving context.

Expected interpretation: Ingredient: pasta (required). Meal: dinner. Exclusion: mushrooms (absolute)
Expected result: 2-3 pasta dinners with zero mushrooms
Must never happen: Any result containing mushrooms in any form
Why this case: Core exclusion case.

Expected interpretation: Dietary exclusion: dairy (absolute)
Expected result: Dairy-free recipes
Must never happen: A recipe tagged "dairy-free" being excluded because it contains the word dairy
Why this case: Negation collision. Named by engineering as a known failure.

Expected interpretation: Exclusion: tomato (absolute)
Hard filters to apply: dinner main; EXCLUDE tomato and tomatoes
Expected result: Dinner mains with no tomato in any form
Must never happen: A recipe with tomatoes surviving because only the singular was matched
Why this case: Singular/plural handling.

Expected interpretation: Exclusion: mushrooms (absolute), misspelled
Expected result: Chicken dinners with no mushrooms
Must never happen: The exclusion being silently dropped because the term did not resolve
Why this case: Misspelling. Silent failure is the worst outcome.

Expected interpretation: Exclusion: corn (absolute)
Expected result: Corn-free soups
Must never happen: Excluding recipes containing cornstarch or peppercorn
Why this case: Substring collision.

Expected interpretation: Unresolvable exclusion term
Expected result: Results plus an explicit statement that we could not interpret "zorblax"
Must never happen: Results presented as though the exclusion was honored
Why this case: Unresolvable terms must be surfaced not swallowed.

User says: vegetarian dinner, no mushrooms, no eggplant, no tofu, under 15 minutes
Expected interpretation: Multiple stacked absolutes
Hard filters to apply: vegetarian; dinner main; EXCLUDE mushrooms/eggplant/tofu; time <= 15
Expected result: Whatever qualifies, even if that is zero, with a clear statement of what emptied it
Must never happen: Quietly dropping one constraint to return something
Why this case: Over-constrained case. Tests honest failure.

Expected interpretation: Diet stated plainly: vegetarian (absolute)
Expected result: Vegetarian dinner mains only
Must never happen: Any meat or fish appearing
Why this case: Plainly stated diet filters.

User says: I'm vegetarian-ish - what should I make for dinner
Expected interpretation: Hedged diet: ranks rather than filters
Expected result: Mostly vegetarian dinner mains, plus a line saying we are leaning vegetarian not enforcing it
Must never happen: Applying a hard vegetarian filter to someone who said they are flexible
Why this case: Dale's case. Tests tier 2 hedging.

User says: I'm mostly vegetarian but my husband eats meat
Expected interpretation: Hedged diet with explicit exception
Expected result: A mix leaning vegetarian, acknowledged in copy
Must never happen: Filtering out all meat despite the user saying otherwise
Why this case: Same tier as G15 stated a different way.

User says: I'm allergic to shellfish - dinner ideas
Expected interpretation: Allergy: absolute regardless of phrasing
Expected result: Dinner mains with zero shellfish
Must never happen: Shellfish appearing; any softening of this because it was phrased casually
Why this case: Allergy is tier 1 no matter how it is said.

Expected interpretation: Quality: quick, relative to Thanksgiving. Not a number
Expected result: Thanksgiving mains ranked by relative speed
Must never happen: A 30-minute cutoff excluding all Thanksgiving mains
Why this case: Dale's case. Quick is relative to the dish class.

Expected interpretation: Time: 120 min (required - a number filters)
Expected result: Thanksgiving mains at or under 2 hours
Must never happen: A 3-hour recipe appearing
Why this case: Same domain as G18 but a number makes it absolute.

Expected interpretation: Baseline
Expected result: 2-3 chicken dinner mains
Why this case: Sets up G21-G23.

Expected interpretation: Additive exclusion
Expected result: New set; chicken and dinner still hold; no pork
Must never happen: Losing the chicken or dinner constraint; returning the same 3 recipes
Why this case: Constraints accumulate across turns.

Expected interpretation: Additive hard time filter
Hard filters to apply: chicken; dinner main; EXCLUDE pork; time <= 30
Expected result: New set honoring all four
Must never happen: Dropping the pork exclusion the user did not repeat
Why this case: Silent constraint loss is the classic multi-turn bug.

Expected interpretation: Replacement: vegetarian replaces chicken. Other constraints persist
Hard filters to apply: vegetarian; dinner main; EXCLUDE pork; time <= 30
Expected result: Vegetarian dinner mains under 30 minutes
Must never happen: Searching for vegetarian chicken; losing the time filter
Why this case: Replacement vs addition. The key ambiguity rule.

Expected interpretation: Soft modifier stacked on prior request
Expected result: New set honoring everything prior plus a cost preference
Must never happen: A hard price filter; losing prior constraints
Why this case: Quality words stack rather than replace.

Expected interpretation: Novelty request; constraints unchanged
Expected result: 3 recipes not previously shown in this conversation
Must never happen: Any recipe from the previous set reappearing; loosening a constraint to find new ones
Why this case: Novelty tracking.

Expected interpretation: Novelty request with a nearly exhausted pool
Expected result: Whatever remains, with a clear statement when it is the last of them
Must never happen: Recycling the first set as though it were new
Why this case: Exhaustion must be honest.

Expected interpretation: Source: saves. Filter: chicken. Sort: time ascending
Expected result: User's saved chicken recipes sorted fastest first
Must never happen: Any catalog recipe appearing; incorrect ordering
Why this case: Core saves query.

User says: that quick pasta puttanesca I saved with cherry tomatoes
Expected interpretation: Source: saves. Anchor: puttanesca. Cherry tomatoes and quick are recall cues not filters
Expected result: The user's puttanesca recipe, even though it has plum tomatoes and no quick tag
Must never happen: Returning nothing because the descriptive terms were applied as filters
Why this case: Dale's case. Saves is recall not filtering.

User says: my vegetarian saves, nothing with mushrooms
Expected interpretation: Source: saves. Diet and exclusion both absolute even in saves
Expected result: Saved vegetarian recipes with no mushrooms
Must never happen: Mushrooms appearing
Why this case: Diet and exclusions still filter in saves. G28 does not weaken this.

Expected interpretation: Requires cook data we do not have
Expected result: A plain statement that we cannot tell yet
Must never happen: Substituting save date or view count and presenting it as cooking history
Why this case: Unanswerable query must be honest.

User says: show me my saves from last month
Expected interpretation: Source: saves. Sort/filter: save date
Hard filters to apply: saves only; saved within date range
Expected result: Saves from that period
Must never happen: Catalog results
Why this case: Date-based saves query.

User says: show me chicken recipes from my saves
Expected interpretation: Explicit source overrides the screen
Expected result: User's saved chicken recipes
Must never happen: Searching the full catalog because the request came from Home
Why this case: Explicit source beats screen context.

User says: find me a new pasta recipe
Expected interpretation: Explicit intent (new) overrides the screen
Expected result: Catalog pasta recipes
Must never happen: Restricting to saves because the request came from Saves
Why this case: The reverse of G32.

Expected interpretation: No explicit source. Screen decides: saves
Expected result: Saved dinner recipes ranked by speed
Must never happen: Silently searching the whole catalog
Why this case: Screen supplies the default when nothing is stated.

Expected interpretation: User has zero saves
Expected result: An honest empty state offering to search all recipes
Must never happen: Catalog recipes presented as the user's saves
Why this case: Empty library.

User says: dinner with no salt no oil no onions no garlic no dairy no gluten
Expected interpretation: Over-constrained
Expected result: An honest miss naming what emptied the set, with an offer to drop one
Must never happen: Silently relaxing an exclusion
Why this case: Constraint stacking to zero.

User says: Turn 1: vegetarian dinner / Turn 2: something for a party / Turn 3: breakfast ideas
Expected interpretation: Topic changed twice; diet persists across both
Expected result: Vegetarian breakfast ideas unaffected by the party context
Must never happen: Party or dinner context bleeding into breakfast; losing the vegetarian constraint
Why this case: Context pollution. Diet survives a topic change; everything else does not.

Expected interpretation: Suggestions derived from the returned set
Expected result: Up to 3 suggestions, each traceable to evidence and each returning results when tapped
Must never happen: "Quick recipes" (restates the request); "Healthy recipes" (no evidence); any suggestion returning zero results
Why this case: Follow-up quality. See the relevance rules spec.

Expected interpretation: Thin set from a dietary constraint
Expected result: Suggestions that move within the constraint
Must never happen: Any suggestion offering to relax the vegetarian constraint
Why this case: Never offer to loosen a dietary restriction.

User says: After a saves query returns 9 results
Expected interpretation: Library too small for refinement
Expected result: No follow-up suggestions
Must never happen: Offering to narrow 9 recipes
Why this case: Follow-ups on saves are gated by library size.

Expected interpretation: Immediate dinner recommendation request; no ingredient intake
Ranking signals: Flavor Profile; inferred makability; recipe quality
Expected result: 3 dinner mains returned immediately
Must never happen: Asking for ingredients before returning value; claiming the user has specific ingredients
Why this case: Tests the new immediate-results dinner flow.

User says: After results, user says: I'd like to use chicken and broccoli
Expected interpretation: Explicit ingredient requirements refine the next set
Ranking signals: Flavor Profile; inferred makability; recipe quality
Expected result: A new dinner set in which every qualifying recipe uses chicken and broccoli
Must never happen: Treating either ingredient as only a soft boost; dropping taste and quality ranking after enforcing them
Why this case: Tests optional post-result ingredient refinement.

User says: After results, user says: must use the chicken
Expected interpretation: Explicit ingredient stated as mandatory
Ranking signals: Flavor Profile; inferred makability; recipe quality
Expected result: A new dinner set in which every recipe uses chicken
Must never happen: Treating chicken as only a soft preference; forgetting other active constraints
Why this case: Tests the difference between include and must use.

User says: Tap Dinner Tonight; user has little or no behavioral history
Expected interpretation: Immediate dinner request with weak personalization and makability evidence
Expected result: 3 strong dinner mains without a pantry claim
Must never happen: Blocking on missing history; pretending to know what the user has
Why this case: Tests cold-start fallback.

User says: I want to make a casserole with mushrooms, rice and cheese
Expected interpretation: Primary dish: casserole. Required ingredients: mushrooms, rice, and cheese
Ranking signals: dish relevance; ingredient centrality; taxonomy; quality; popularity
Expected result: Complete matches that are casseroles and contain mushrooms, rice, and cheese
Must never happen: Returning a casserole without one ingredient; returning a non-casserole just because its ingredient list contains all four words
Why this case: Core distinction between dish and required ingredients.

User says: I want to make a casserole with mushrooms, rice and cheese
Expected interpretation: Primary dish: casserole. Required ingredients: mushrooms, rice, and cheese; Parmesan satisfies cheese
Hard filters to apply: casserole; mushrooms; rice; cheese or normalized subtype
Expected result: A casserole with mushrooms, rice, and Parmesan qualifies
Must never happen: Rejecting Parmesan because the literal word cheese is absent
Why this case: Tests ingredient equivalence and parent/subtype normalization.

User says: I want to make a casserole with mushrooms, rice and cheese
Expected interpretation: Only one complete match exists; partial matches also exist
Expected result: The one complete match first; partial matches separately identified with the missing ingredient
Must never happen: Mixing partials into the qualifying set without labeling; padding the main set to three
Why this case: Tests controlled fallback.

Expected interpretation: Primary dish and required ingredient are ambiguous
Expected result: One clarifying question if the structure cannot be resolved reliably
Must never happen: Arbitrarily enforcing the wrong concept as the dish or ingredient
Why this case: Tests ambiguity handling.

Expected interpretation: Primary dish: pasta. Required ingredients: spinach and ricotta
Expected result: Complete matches, with recipes centered on spinach and ricotta ranked above incidental uses
Must never happen: Allowing incidental ingredient hits to outrank a clearly matching dish
Why this case: Tests presence as gate and centrality as ranking.
